newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly up on Thursday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,600 yuan ($2,821) per tonne, rising 80 yuan.
It opened at 23,600 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 23,670 and a low of 23,590.
June was unchanged at 22,650, July rose 40 to 22,940, August added 20 to 23,180, September was unchanged at 23,400, November rose 120 to 23,620 and December fell 370 to 23,600.
Combined volume rose to 45,940 tonnes from 33,120.
Copper opened higher on the LME gains but fell steadily for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said speculative buying continued to emerge on Thursday but the contracts met strong resistance at high levels, in the same way as Wednesday.

"Large amounts of long liquidation and fresh selling at high levels made copper fall steadily for most of the session today," one trader said. "Many investors are pessimistic about the short-term market trend despite today's rises."
Physical prices are around 22,900 yuan in the Shanghai area, down from 23,000 last week.
Analysts said there was little potential for further rises, especially of late-maturing contracts, due to weak sentiment.

"Many investors believe copper will not rise above the 24,000-yuan level since it failed to breach the level one week ago," a second trader said. "the siruation is not clear enough to build long positions at the current level."
Aluminium ended mixed. June fell 30 to 14,550, July did not trade, August dropped 100 to 14,950, September rose 100 to 15,050 and October put on 100 to 15,050.
Combined volume fell to 1,780 tonnes from 2,820.
